purpose: Define the lifecycle organ's interface layers, adapter boundaries, sovereign Forgejo boundary, and runtime surfaces so agents can extend the organ without reintroducing implicit coupling.

scope.boundary: Ports are the only supported integration surface between the lifecycle core and external systems.

forge_boundary.git_role: content-addressed repository substrate and local membrane
forge_boundary.github_role: external proprietary upstream, backup, publication and intelligence source; not the priority agency/privacy lifecycle authority
forge_boundary.required_property: Forge operations must cross a port and produce Kernel-readable evidence before lifecycle state advances.

adapter_map.responsibility: Load registry desired state and resolve nodes or services without hardcoded paths.
Read fleet truth from the declared Surreal-backed mesh surface.
Read service registry health from the kernel's declared service surface.
Read storage-primary health and produce backup bundles through the kernel contract.
Build and dispatch lifecycle requests through the kernel mempool surface.
Register, claim, release, and read coordination state through the kernel coord API.
Record observations and read lifecycle observations through the kernel observability surface.
Analyze supply-chain dependencies, execution order, and circular references from registry truth.

constraints: No cortex-local build is part of this contract.
Adapters must be thin and single-responsibility.
Registry loading must flow through the registry port, not ad hoc json parsing in business logic.
Kernel coordination and observation must use declared REST or MCP-backed ports.
Forgejo operations must not be hidden behind generic GitHub or pull-request assumptions.
Every lifecycle transition must preserve the recursive shape: intent, claim, route, execute, observe, result, converge.
